motivation.text: A plain transform scans $\Theta(n)$ bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ levels, already $\Theta(n\log n)$, so both the data movement and the arithmetic must be made cheaper than a full pass per level.

motivation.text: Each phase costs a bounded number of passes times a factor that is a power of $p$ below one, so comparing exponents with $1$ shows which phase limits the saving.

adds.name: normalizing volume
adds.meaning: the stored bit volume $Tp=\Theta(n)$ by which all costs are divided.

adds.name: exponent margin
adds.meaning: the amount by which the $i$th dominant normalized cost is a power of $p$ below one, $i=1,\ldots,7$.

children.salient: The saving exponent $\kappa=2^{-182}$ is astronomically small and equals half the smallest margin, $g_2=\epsilon c(1-\tau)=2^{-75}\cdot2^{-56}\cdot2^{-50}=2^{-181}$, a product of three tiny exponents coming from the chunk-exchange term $pK^{\tau-1}$; the other six margins are all larger.
